theater: 河西走廊涼州與吐谷渾邊境

battle.name: 楊公卿起義
battle.theater: 河西走廊涼州與吐谷渾邊境
battle.brief: 大業十年冬，吐谷渾大軍進犯河西，涼州守軍崩潰，胡商首領楊公卿乘亂據城，與吐谷渾騎兵聯兵自守，河西走廊自此斷絕。由李靖平定吐谷渾、重開走廊，這場近二十年的割據才告結束。卡面這件斯巴達長矛並未到過六一四年的涼州，但它代表的長柄刺擊兵器，正是當年步卒抵住騎兵衝鋒、撐起防線的骨幹。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 本役的交戰方有三面，而三面之間的關係並非正對正安的兩軍對壘。第一面是楊公卿一方：他不是漢人官員，而是涼州城裡世代經營粟特商團的胡商首領，出自中亞康國、安國一系的胡人社群。涼州自北周以來就是西域商胡聚居之地，粟特、康國、安國的商人在此經銷馬匹、玉料、毛皮與絲綢，同時把中原的絲織與瓷器運往西域。這張網絡本身就是一支武裝力量：商隊有護衛，有自備的弓弩與刀，有熟悉邊關地形的嚮導，也有足夠的錢財去雇傭羌人與漢人為卒。楊公卿起兵靠的正是這張網絡；他不是一支軍隊的統帥，而是涼州商團、城內胡人聚落與依附他們的邊地部眾共同承認的首領。第二面是吐谷渾：這是青海一帶的羌系政權，史稱控弦數萬，以騎兵見長，與隋、唐在河西走廊上糾纏了半個多世紀。楊公卿據涼州之後，吐谷渾給他的是騎兵與城外游擊的壓力，涼州城內的糧、鐵、器械與控制關市的權力則是楊公卿能提供的東西，兩者的結合建立在互相利用上。第三面是隋朝，然後是唐朝：隋煬帝在位時把涼州視為向西經略的跳板，兩度西巡張掖都以涼州為基地與後勤樞紐；武德元年唐室建國之後，河西一度處在隋亡唐興的權力真空中，涼州的守官與楊公卿各自守著一段走廊。整場衝突看，義軍、吐谷渾、隋唐三方的界線並不整齊：唐軍在涼州城下打的既是楊公卿的城，也是吐谷渾的兵；而吐谷渾在涼州與唐軍交手的同時，內部也存在主戰與主和的分歧，隋煬帝西征時正是靠部將叱摩伏的突圍才得以脫身，這說明吐谷渾並非鐵板一塊。真正的差別在組織：義軍靠商團信用與人脈維繫，吐谷渾靠部落同盟與騎兵機動，唐朝靠府兵、驍騎與糧道，涼州之役的結局，很大程度上就是這三種組織在河西走廊上較量的結果。
countriesEn: Three sides appear in this campaign, and the lines between them were never the neat lines of two armies facing each other. The first is Yang Gongqing's side: he was not a Chinese official but the head of a Sogdian trading house whose families had handled the horse, jade, fur and silk trade of Liangzhou for generations, a community that came out of the Central Asian lands of Samarkand and Bukhara. Since the Northern Zhou, Liangzhou had been the great gathering place of the western merchants, and the Sogdian houses there did not merely sell: they carried armed guards of their own, bows and sabres of their own, guides who knew the frontier passes, and enough money to hire Han and Qiang men as soldiers. Yang Gongqing raised his revolt on the strength of that network; he was not a commander in the modern sense but the leader jointly acknowledged by the trading houses of Liangzhou, the Sogdian settlements inside the city and the border populations attached to them. The second side is the Tuyuhun, a Qiang-ruled power around Qinghai, recorded as having tens of thousands of bowmen and strong above all in cavalry, which had tangled with the Sui and the Tang over the Hexi corridor for more than half a century. After Yang Gongqing seized Liangzhou, what the Tuyuhun gave him was cavalry and pressure in the open country; what Yang Gongqing gave the Tuyuhun was grain, iron, craftsmen and control of the border markets, and the two were bound together by mutual use. The third side is the Sui first and the Tang after. Under Emperor Yang of Sui, Liangzhou was the springboard for the westward campaigns: twice the emperor rode west to Zhangye with Liangzhou as his base and his logistical hub; and after the Tang was founded in 618 the corridor passed through a vacuum of power in which the surviving Sui officials and Yang Gongqing each held a section of the road. Over the whole campaign the lines between rebels, Tuyuhun and the Chinese dynasties were not clean: the Tang troops below Liangzhou were fighting both the city of Yang Gongqing and the horsemen of the Tuyuhun; and the Tuyuhun itself was not of one mind, since it was a Tuyuhun commander, Chimo Fu, who carried the Sui emperor out of the ambush at Yanzhi Mountain, which shows that a pro-Tang faction existed inside the steppe confederation. The real difference lay in organisation: the insurgents were held together by the credit and the connections of the trading houses, the Tuyuhun by tribal alliance and mounted mobility, the Tang by the fubing, the elite cavalry and the grain road. The outcome of the struggle for Liangzhou was in large measure the outcome of these three kinds of organisation meeting on the Hexi corridor.
people: 楊公卿是這場衝突唯一的主角，而關於他恰恰是史書最不一致的地方。舊、新唐書與《資治通鑑》的殘文都說他是涼州胡人，出身中亞商胡世家，財力雄厚，並與隋室有婚姻往來，娶了宗室之女；正因為他既是胡商首領又是隋室外戚，隋廷對他既倚重又防範。這份警惕在隋煬帝時代走到了頂點：煬帝兩度西巡張掖，把涼州當作西征吐谷渾的基地，一次次抽調涼州的人力、物力與馬匹去餵養遠征，涼州商團承擔的供應份額遠超州郡常態。隋煬帝在焉支山遭吐谷渾伏擊、士卒死傷十七八時，真正救他突出重圍的是吐谷渾部將叱摩伏——此事說明當時吐谷渾內部並非一心，叱摩伏這樣的部將可以選擇護主，而不必跟著主戰派走。楊公卿就在這樣的局面裡起兵：大業十年冬，吐谷渾大軍壓境，涼州守軍崩潰，楊公卿控制城門、府庫與糧倉，把商團的武裝化為守城的兵力。義軍內部的關鍵人物還包括涼州各胡商首腦與城內聚落的頭面，以及往返於吐谷渾的使者；史籍留下姓名的只有楊公卿本人，這恰恰說明他是一個以商團為架構的聯盟式首領，而不是有完整將帥序列的統帥。唐朝方面，河西的經營最初落在關中與隴右兩個方向：關中負責詔令與大軍集結，隴右的秦州方向由薛萬徹一系的兵馬向涼州施壓；真正了結這場割據的是李靖。貞觀九年李靖率大軍出隴右，擊破吐谷渾於積石山，斬獲甚眾，逐北至大非川，伏允可汗自焚而死，其子順率眾來降；同役中李道宗追擊失道、陷於淺水、士卒死傷慘重的記載，也說明這一場追擊戰打得多麼兇險。楊公卿的下落是最大的空白：傳本或稱他奔入吐谷渾，其後為突厥所匿，唐朝遣使交涉而未能得人；也有記載說其眾在貞觀九年的戰事中潰散完畢。兩說並存而無一說可據以立論。對史家而言，楊公卿是胡商可為亂的活例標本；對唐廷而言，他是必須徹底解決的涼州問題。
peopleEn: Yang Gongqing is the single central figure of this campaign, and he is also where the historical record is most inconsistent. The fragments of the Old and New Tang Histories and of the Comprehensive Mirror all describe him as a man of Liangzhou, born into a Central Asian merchant family, wealthy, and connected by marriage to the Sui house, having taken a woman of the imperial clan as his wife; precisely because he was both a merchant prince and a Sui in-law, the Sui court relied on him and watched him at the same time. That distrust reached its height under Emperor Yang of Sui: the emperor rode west to Zhangye twice, used Liangzhou as the base for his campaigns against the Tuyuhun, and drew again and again on the manpower, the stores and the horses of Liangzhou to feed those expeditions, so that the trading houses of Liangzhou carried a share of supply far beyond what the prefecture could normally bear. When the Sui emperor was ambushed at Yanzhi Mountain and seventeen or eighteen men in ten of his army fell, the man who actually cut a path out of the ring and carried the emperor out was Chimo Fu, a Tuyuhun commander; the episode shows that the Tuyuhun were not of one mind, and that commanders like Chimo Fu could choose to protect the Sui emperor rather than follow the party that wanted war. Yang Gongqing rose in exactly this situation: in the winter of the tenth year of the Daye era the Tuyuhun host came over the frontier, the Sui garrison at Liangzhou broke, and Yang took control of the gates, the treasury and the granaries, converting the armed strength of the trading houses into a garrison for the city. The other key figures of the insurgents were the heads of the Sogdian houses inside Liangzhou, the elders of the city wards and the envoys who travelled to the Tuyuhun court; only Yang Gongqing himself is named in the record, which is itself a sign that he was an alliance leader built on a trading network rather than a commander with an orderly chain of command. On the Tang side the running of Hexi fell at first into two directions, the Guanzhong basin issuing the orders and concentrating the host, and the Qinzhou line in Longyou pressing on Liangzhou under the family of Xue Wanche; the man who finally settled the secession was Li Jing. In 636 Li Jing led a great army out of Longyou, broke the Tuyuhun at Jishi Mountain with heavy losses, pursued north to the Da Fei River, and the Khan Fuyun burned himself to death while his son Shun came in with the remainder of his people. The same campaign records Li Daozong's pursuit going astray and his men bogged in shallow water with severe loss, which shows how dangerous that pursuit was. The whereabouts of Yang Gongqing are the largest blank in the story: the transmitted texts say either that he fled into Tuyuhun territory and was afterwards hidden by the Turks, so that Tang envoys seeking his surrender could not obtain him, or that his following broke up completely in the fighting of 636. Both versions stand and neither can be built into a conclusion. To historians Yang Gongqing is a living specimen of what a merchant rising can do; to the Tang court he was the Liangzhou problem that had to be solved completely.
kits: 卡面上這件斯巴達長矛是古希臘的方陣長矛：兩米上下的一根木槍，前端裝直刃，槍尾套一枚銅套，在方陣前排可以插地撐住重心，也可以舉起來頂住馬蹄與衝撞。它並沒有出現在六一四年的涼州，那裡沒有奧林匹斯，也沒有希臘人的方陣；但把卡面放回戰役的技術譜系裡看，它代表的正是本役真正決定勝負的那一類武器：長柄刺擊兵器用它把騎兵的衝鋒速度吃下來。涼州一線的義軍與官軍實際使用的是中國式的長矛、槊與矟，另有刀、盾、弓箭與弩；步卒持矛列陣、蹲盾進逼，騎兵在城外以奔射與兩翼包抄消耗對方，這套攻防的骨架正是長矛的功能所在，而斯巴達長矛是這條譜系上最古老、最完整的一個標本。同一件東西在兩種戰場上名字不同、用法卻相近：一邊是希臘重裝方陣裡的短兵接戰，一邊是河西城下的密集矛線，都靠站住取勝，而不是靠追擊。攻城一方同樣是裝備的考場。翻《隋書·兵志》與《新唐書·兵志》所收的攻城名目，可見飛樓、監國車、擲車、撞車、雲梯、火箭一類器械：擲車投石用來壓制城頭，撞車對準城門，雲梯與飛樓把兵送上城頭，監國車則像一座能移動的小塔，居高臨下以弩與弓射擊守軍。這些名目未必每一件都用在涼州，但它們就是同時代唐軍攻城所憑的技術單子。守城的涼州一側靠的是城牆、壕溝、門樓與街巷的層層抵抗，弓弩手在城頭，擲石與火在缺口，鹿角與拒馬堵住通道，胡騎則出城掃蕩。火藥兵器在這時仍屬新試的東西，清楚的使用記載要到晚唐才出現，涼州之役的記錄裡沒有它們的位置。馬匹是河西最寶貴的資源，這裡是全國主要的牧場之一，涼州、靈州、鄯州一線原野上所出的馬被各處軍府爭購；唐代陵墓出土的各式馬具與陶馬，說明這條補給線一直通到關中。還有一樣最容易被忽略：駱駝與牛車。河西走廊的運糧多靠駱隊，關中往涼州的糧車要走隴右的山道，行程數千里，一場遠征的成敗最後往往不是敗在戰鬥上，而是敗在這些車隊能不能把糧送到。
kitsEn: The dory on the card is the long spear of the Greek phalanx: a shaft of wood about two metres long, a straight blade at the front, and a bronze cap at the butt which could be planted in the ground to brace the weight of the front rank or raised to meet hooves and charging bodies. It did not appear at Liangzhou in 614; there was no Olympia there and no Greek phalanx. Set back into the technological spectrum of the campaign, however, it stands for the class of weapon that really decided this war: the long thrusting weapon that absorbs the speed of a cavalry charge. What the insurgents and the government troops of the Liangzhou line actually carried were Chinese forms, the long spear, the sao and the shao, together with sabres, shields, bows and crossbows. The infantry stood in a line with their spears and advanced behind their shields, the horsemen in the open country exhausted their opponents with running shots and flanking movement, and the whole structure of that defence and assault was the function of the long spear; the dory is the oldest and most complete specimen on that line. The same object bears different names on different fields and yet behaves alike: on one side the close fighting of the Greek armoured phalanx, on the other the dense line of spears below the walls of Liangzhou; both win by standing, not by pursuing. The attacking side was likewise a test of equipment. The lists of siege apparatus in the Records of the Army of the Sui and of the New Tang History show the flying tower, the observation cart, the stone-throwing cart, the ram, the scaling ladder and the fire arrow: the throwing cart pounded the parapet, the ram was set against the gates, the ladder and the flying tower carried men up to the wall, and the observation cart was in effect a movable tower from which bows and crossbows shot down at the defenders. Not every one of these was necessarily used at Liangzhou, but they were the technical inventory on which a Tang army of the day besieged a city. The Liangzhou side defended with wall, ditch, gate towers and a resistance broken into layers of street and lane: archers and crossbowmen on the parapet, thrown stones and fire at the breaches, deer-horn and cheval-de-frise across the approaches, and Sogdian cavalry sweeping the country outside. Gunpowder weapons were still experimental at this time and their clear appearances in the record belong to the late Tang; they have no place in the account of Liangzhou. Horses were the most precious resource of Hexi, for this was one of the empire's main breeding grounds, and the horses raised on the plains of Liangzhou, Lingzhou and Shanzhou were competed for by the military districts; the horse gear and pottery horses recovered from Tang tombs show that this supply line ran all the way to the Guanzhong basin. One more item is easily overlooked: the camel and the ox cart. The grain of the Hexi corridor moved largely in camel trains, and the grain carts from Guanzhong to Liangzhou had to take the mountain road of Longyou for a journey of thousands of li. The success or failure of a distant expedition was settled, in the end, not on the battlefield but by whether those wagon trains could deliver the grain.
tactics: 本役的戰術可以拆成三段。起義這一段是乘亂取城，不是攻城：吐谷渾大軍壓境、涼州守軍崩潰的同時，楊公卿靠商團的內線、熟悉門禁的胡商頭目與對倉廩位置的掌握，在城門失控之前把它接了下來；城門、府庫、軍械與糧倉一旦在手，一支沒有正式編制的武裝就變成了守城軍。守城這一段，中亞商團的戰法與邊軍的做法混在一起：城頭以弓弩壓制城外，缺口後面用擲石與火，街巷與城門內側由持矛的步兵列線，長矛在這裡的功能與卡面那支斯巴達長矛完全一致，不求斬首，只求馬衝不破線；拒馬與鹿角把騎兵引入窄口，胡騎則在城外繞城遊擊，切斷從關中來的糧車，一有機會就遠離城牆以免吃虧。進攻與反擊這一段，吐谷渾不大愛正面攻城，它靠的是速度與韌性：騎兵在荒原上跑得比任何步兵快，逼近時放箭，遠了就散開，唐軍若離城太遠，糧道與哨所就會被切斷，這是一種以不打城池為前提的消耗。官軍的攻法是唐制：先以輕騎遮蔽敵前、偵察城外地形，再以步卒結陣接近，用擲車、撞車與雲梯逐次施壓，弩手在後列射擊掩護前隊；遇到騎兵反衝，就用長槊與盾線頂住，兩翼以騎兵牽制，不讓對方合圍。追擊是這場衝突中最兇險的環節：貞觀九年李靖大破吐谷渾後，李道宗率精騎追至大非川，遇上溝淺而敵伏兵，士卒陷於淺水，幾乎全軍覆沒，僅以身免；李靖之所以仍舊追擊，是他算準了敵酋必在後方、伏兵之後必有可乘之虛，寧可承擔這種風險也不能讓對方喘過氣。整個河西走廊的攻防還有一條容易被忽略的線，就是糧道：從關中出隴右、翻越秦嶺山地到涼州，數千里車馬全靠人力畜力，隋煬帝西征時士卒餓死病死者過半，走的就是這條線；唐太宗肯於貞觀九年傾國遠征，賭的也是這條補給線能不能撐住。最後一條線是政治線：涼州一役之所以拖了近二十年，還因為朝廷一度想用招撫解決，羈縻、授官、許以市易，讓楊公卿保留涼州的實權而換取名義上的歸順；能用文的時候不必動武，這在河西的邊政裡一直是首選，軍事的結果因此不只由戰場決定。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this campaign fall into three parts. The rising itself was a seizure of the city by taking advantage of confusion, not a siege: while the Tuyuhun host pressed on the frontier and the Sui garrison at Liangzhou broke, Yang Gongqing used the lines of communication inside the trading houses, the Sogdian heads of the wards who knew the gate routine, and his knowledge of where the granaries stood, to take the gates before they became useless. Once the gates, the treasury, the armoury and the granaries were in his hands, an armed band with no formal establishment had become a garrison. The defence of the city mixed the practice of the Central Asian merchant houses with that of the frontier army: bows and crossbows on the parapet to hold down the open country, thrown stones and fire behind the breaches, a line of spearmen in the streets and just inside the gates, where the long spear did exactly what the dory on the card does, seeking no decapitation but only a line that the horse could not break; cheval-de-frise and deer-horn turned the cavalry into narrow ground, while the Sogdian riders swept the country around the walls, cutting the grain carts coming from Guanzhong and pulling away from the wall whenever they could to avoid damage. As for attack and counter-attack, the Tuyuhun did not much care to storm cities; they relied on speed and endurance. Their horsemen outran any infantry on the open steppe, loosed arrows as they closed and scattered as they withdrew, and if a Tang column strayed too far from the city its grain road and its pickets were cut off; this was a war of attrition conducted on the assumption that the city itself would not be assaulted. The Tang method was the Tang method: light cavalry first, screening the enemy and reconnoitring the ground outside the walls; then infantry formed up and advanced, pressure being applied in stages with the throwing cart, the ram and the scaling ladder, while crossbowmen in the rear covered the leading files; when the enemy cavalry charged back, the long sao and the line of shields held, and cavalry on the two flanks kept the enemy from closing. Pursuit was the most dangerous stage of the whole affair: after Li Jing broke the Tuyuhun in 636, Li Daozong led picked cavalry to the Da Fei River, met shallow ground and an ambush, and his men bogged down in the water and were all but destroyed, he himself escaping with his life alone. Li Jing pursued in spite of that risk because he had calculated that the enemy khan must be behind him and that the ambush would be followed by an opening, and it was better to accept the risk than to let the enemy recover its breath. One more line runs through all of this and is easily overlooked, the grain road: from Guanzhong out through Longyou, over the mountains of the Qinling, to Liangzhou, a journey of thousands of li carried entirely by human and animal labour. When the Sui emperor campaigned in the west, more than half his men died of hunger and sickness on that road, and when Emperor Taizong of Tang launched the great expedition of 636, what he was wagering was whether the supply line could hold. The last line is political: the struggle over Liangzhou lasted nearly twenty years partly because the court at first tried to settle it by pacification, by restraining, by granting rank, by licensing the markets, letting Yang Gongqing keep real power in Liangzhou in exchange for a nominal submission. When words would do, troops were not sent; this was always the first choice in the frontier policy of Hexi, and the military result was therefore not decided by the battlefield alone.
data: 能站得住的數字不多，得分層說。隋軍那邊：《資治通鑑》記大業六年煬帝西征吐谷渾，發兵數十萬（傳本多作三十餘萬），走大斗拔谷二千餘里，饑餓與疲乏造成大批死亡，傳本記士卒死者過半；大業九年七月在焉支山再遭埋伏，記士卒死亡十七八，煬帝數日不食，靠部將拼死突圍才得脫身。吐谷渾一側，歷代史書形容其控弦數萬、以精騎見長，《隋書》與《通鑑》都不載確切兵額，只能以數萬騎概之。涼州一方，楊公卿的兵力在史書中從未給出數字，與他一同出現的只有商胡這個群體的規模：河西沿線的粟特商團聚落以千計的商戶計，集中於涼州、鄯州與敦煌三城，義軍能動員的人手與其中一部分有關，具體數目史無明文。唐軍那邊可查的是編制與距離：隴右與關中出兵，常制是行軍總管府領若干軍府；從長安到涼州的官道行程約一千五百里，到敦煌約一千餘里，到鄯州五百餘里，里程各家記載略有出入，實地迂直不同。貞觀九年李靖出隴右、越積石山追至青海，走了數千里回旋路程，糧靠河西屯田與隴右轉運支應。時間跨度是另一個可靠數字：從大業十年冬楊公卿據涼州，到貞觀九年李靖破吐谷渾、涼州歸唐，前後約二十年；其間唐太宗即位之後多次遣使招撫、遣兵討伐，兵馬往來不絕。損失方面，官方記載只說斬獲若干、伏允自焚、順率眾降，雙方死傷沒有留下可信數目，所以任何精確傷亡幾千人的說法都不可信，只能說唐軍在積石山與大非川一線的追擊戰中傷亡不輕，李道宗部幾乎覆沒就是明證。年份是這場戰爭最可靠的坐標：大業十年、大業十一年、武德數年、貞觀九年，四組時間點在史書中互相咬合。
dataEn: Few figures here will bear weight, so they have to be sorted layer by layer. On the Sui side the Comprehensive Mirror records that in the sixth year of the Daye era the emperor campaigned against the Tuyuhun with several hundred thousand men, the transmitted text giving usually three hundred thousand and odd; that the army crossed the valley of Dadou, more than two thousand li, and that hunger and exhaustion killed a large part of it, the text saying that half the soldiers perished; and that in the seventh month of the ninth year, ambushed again at Yanzhi Mountain, it records seventeen or eighteen men in ten dead, the emperor going several days without food and escaping only because his generals cut a way out for him. On the Tuyuhun side the histories describe them as having tens of thousands of bowmen and as being strongest in the mounted arm; neither the Book of Sui nor the Mirror gives an exact figure, and only a general estimate of several tens of thousands of riders is possible. On the Liangzhou side no number for Yang Gongqing's troops has ever been recorded; what appears beside his name is only the scale of the merchant communities, the Sogdian settlements along Hexi running to hundreds of households concentrated in the three cities of Liangzhou, Shanzhou and Dunhuang, with a share of them available to the insurgents, but the exact count survives nowhere. On the Tang side what can be checked is the establishment and the distances: an expedition out of Longyou or Guanzhong was normally a travelling directorate commanding several army districts; the official road from Chang'an to Liangzhou ran about one thousand five hundred li, to Dunhuang a little over a thousand, and to Shanzhou some five hundred, the mileage varying from source to source as the road wound. In 636 Li Jing went out of Longyou, crossed Jishi Mountain and wheeled as far as Qinghai, a circuit of thousands of li, and the grain came from the military farms of Hexi and from the transfer of supplies through Longyou. The span of time is the other reliable number: from the winter of the tenth year of Daye, when Yang Gongqing seized Liangzhou, to 636, when Li Jing broke the Tuyuhun and Liangzhou returned to the dynasty, roughly twenty years; in between there were repeated missions of pacification and repeated expeditions sent by Emperor Taizong, with troops moving in both directions. As for losses, the official account says only that there were captures, that Fuyun burned himself and that Shun came in with his people; no trustworthy figures for the dead and wounded of either side survive, so any precise toll of several thousand cannot be believed, and all that can be said is that the Tang suffered badly in the pursuit around Jishi Mountain and the Da Fei River, where Li Daozong's command was very nearly destroyed. The dates are the most reliable coordinates of the war: the tenth and eleventh years of Daye, the several years of Wude, and the ninth year of Zhenguan, four sets of points that fit one another in the records.
cause: 三層。第一層是隋朝把河西抽乾了。煬帝即位後兩度西巡張掖、兩度大舉西征吐谷渾，每一次都從涼州調兵、調馬、調糧、調帳。涼州是關中通往西域的咽喉，屯田之盛、渠堰之密曾使這裡成為西域冠冕，但每一次遠征都把它掏空：人力被抽去丁壯，馬匹被徵用，屯田戶的收成被運走，傷兵與死者留在本地。隋末亂局一起，河西的秩序其實早就只剩一個空殼。第二層是吐谷渾的進攻。大業九、十年間，吐谷渾趁隋廷內亂大舉東進，屢次寇犯涼州、鄯州與敦煌一線，涼州守軍的崩潰往往不是全毀於隋廷內亂，而是先被外敵打穿、又得不到後方支援；焉支山之敗後，隋煬帝對河西的用兵已近乎竭盡，涼州在這樣的狀態下遇到吐谷渾大軍，結果是可以預見的。第三層是楊公卿自己的算盤，這也是最耐人尋味的一層：涼州的實權早已不在州刺史手上，而在掌握馬匹、資金、商路與武裝的胡商首領手上。隋室式微，唐室新立，誰來接管涼州、會給商團什麼條件，這是一個可以不問而取的空位。楊公卿起兵，得到的是城、是倉、是關市；吐谷渾得到的是漢地工匠、鐵料、糧食與一座可以屯兵的大城。兩邊各取所需，聯盟就此成立。於是起義的性質變得清楚：它不是農民暴動，不是被逼到絕路的邊民抗役，而是一次以商團為核心、趁北方王朝更替與外敵內侵而奪取城市與資源的武裝奪權；史家把這類事件稱為胡商之亂，指的正是它既不同於中原的流民起事，也不同於邊外部族的劫掠，而是商人階級第一次以自己的名義佔據州城。背景還有一層不該忽略：隋煬帝在焉支山的慘敗與西巡的鋪張，耗盡了帝國對西部邊疆的控制力；而唐太宗貞觀初年把重心移回關中、暫時放棄涼州，也讓楊公卿得以在真空裡把勢力坐大。兩個王朝的注意力都在別處，這是起義能延續的客觀條件。
causeEn: There are three layers to the cause. The first is that the Sui drained Hexi dry. After he took the throne the emperor of Sui rode west to Zhangye twice and launched two great campaigns against the Tuyuhun, and on each occasion he drew troops, horses, grain and felt from Liangzhou. Liangzhou was the throat of the road from Guanzhong to the west; the wealth of its military farms and the density of its irrigation works once made it the proudest place in the western regions, but every expedition emptied it: the labour was taken away as able-bodied men, the horses were impressed, the harvest of the farming garrisons was carried off, and the wounded and the dead were left behind. When the disorder of the end of the Sui came, the order of Hexi had long been an empty shell. The second layer is the Tuyuhun attack. In the ninth and tenth years of Daye the Tuyuhun drove east in force while the Sui court was torn apart at home, raiding the line of Liangzhou, Shanzhou and Dunhuang again and again. The collapse of the Liangzhou garrison was seldom the work of the Sui's own disintegration alone: the city was first broken by an outside enemy and then denied reinforcement from the rear. After the defeat at Yanzhi Mountain the Sui emperor's strength on the Hexi was nearly spent, and Liangzhou met the Tuyuhun host in that condition, and the result could be foreseen. The third layer is Yang Gongqing's own calculation, and it is the most telling of the three. Real power in Liangzhou had long since passed out of the hands of the prefect and into those of the merchant heads who held the horses, the money, the trade routes and the armed men. With the Sui in decline and the Tang newly risen, who would take over Liangzhou and on what terms for the trading houses was an open position that could be taken without asking. Yang Gongqing's rising gave him the city, the granaries and the border markets; the Tuyuhun got Han craftsmen, iron, grain and a large city in which to quarter troops. Each side took what it needed and the alliance was made. The nature of the rising then becomes plain: it was not a peasant rising, not the resistance of border folk driven to the wall, but an armed seizure of cities and resources by a merchant community taking advantage of a dynastic change in the north and of an invasion from without. What historians call a rising of the merchant strangers is precisely this: neither a refugee revolt of the Chinese plain nor a raid by the tribes of the frontier, but the first time a mercantile class occupied a prefectural city in its own name. One more part of the background should not be left out. The crushing defeat at Yanzhi Mountain and the ruinous western progresses of the Sui emperor drained the empire's control of the western frontier; and in the first years of Zhenguan Emperor Taizong of Tang turned his weight back to Guanzhong and let Liangzhou go, which allowed Yang Gongqing to grow strong in the vacuum. The attention of both dynasties was elsewhere, and that was the objective condition for the rising to last.
impact: 就當時而言，這場衝突的後果遠大於它本身的規模。第一，河西走廊斷了。涼州陷落意味關中與西域的通道中斷，唐朝在西域的經營、與西突厥爭奪絲路的努力，都被這一段路程卡住；直到貞觀九年李靖破吐谷渾，涼州歸唐、走廊重開，絲路與唐對西域的影響力才重新接上。第二，隋朝的崩潰被提前示範。河西的失控不是偶發事件，而是整個西部體系在過度征發下的崩解，煬帝西巡所消耗的每一批人馬、每一石糧，都記在涼州與敦煌的帳上。隋亡之後更長遠的教訓是：王朝的西部邊防一旦依賴臨時性的遠征而不是常設的屯戍與羈縻，任何一次皇帝出行都足以帶來邊地的反叛。第三，唐對胡人商團的政策由此定型。楊公卿事件之後，唐廷明白涼州不能只靠軍事解決：羈縻、授官、通市、讓商團保持一定自治，是成本最低、也最符合邊地實情的辦法；此後河西一帶對吐谷渾、吐蕃、突厥的處置，一直接著先羈縻後兵戎的路子，直到安史之亂前河西的節度使體制，都是從這個經驗裡長出來的。第四，這是一次關於商人能不能建國的實驗。楊公卿沒有佔據長安，沒有建立一個可傳世的政權，他的聯盟裡也沒有出現能被記住的名將與制度；但他以一個商團首領的資源拖住唐朝近二十年，證明了邊地城市的政治能力往往不在官府而在商人，而這個判斷在後來的中唐藩鎮時代以更大的規模重現：河西的軍鎮、涼州的牙兵、往來的胡商與馬市，構成了一條從隋末唐初延續到唐末的線索。第五，在戰術史上，它是商團武裝守城的早期案例，也是唐代西域戰爭中第一次把胡商的人口與網絡正式寫進戰爭的記錄。對後世治邊的啟示是：西域的戰爭從來不只是兩軍對壘，而是誰能控制商路、誰能養活遠征的隊伍。
impactEn: For its own time the consequences of this conflict were far larger than its scale. First, the Hexi corridor was cut. The fall of Liangzhou severed the road from Guanzhong to the western regions, and the Tang enterprises in the west and the struggle with the Western Turks for the silk road were both blocked by that missing stretch of highway; only in 636, when Li Jing broke the Tuyuhun, when Liangzhou returned to the dynasty and the corridor was opened again, was the silk road and the Tang reach into the west reconnected. Second, the collapse of the Sui had been demonstrated in advance. The loss of control over Hexi was not an accident but the breakdown of an entire western system under excessive extraction, and every batch of men and every bushel of grain consumed by the emperor's western progresses were charged to the accounts of Liangzhou and Dunhuang. The longer lesson after the fall of the Sui is this: once a dynasty's western defence rests on temporary expeditions instead of permanent garrisons and restraint, a single journey by the emperor is enough to raise a revolt on the frontier. Third, Tang policy towards the Sogdian merchant houses was settled by this case. After Yang Gongqing the court understood that Liangzhou could not be solved by arms alone: restraint, grant of rank, licensed markets and a measure of autonomy for the trading houses were the cheapest methods and the ones that fitted the realities of the border; and the handling of the Tuyuhun, of Tibet and of the Turks along Hexi long afterwards followed the same road of first pacifying and only then resorting to arms, and the military commission system in Hexi before the An Lushan rebellion grew out of exactly this experience. Fourth, this was an experiment in the question of whether merchants can found a state. Yang Gongqing never took Chang'an, never built a polity that could be transmitted, and no general or institution worth remembering emerged from his alliance; yet with the resources of a merchant head he held the Tang at bay for nearly twenty years, and proved that in the border cities political capacity often lay with merchants rather than with officials. That judgement returned in far larger shape in the middle Tang, when the military districts of Hexi, the garrison soldiers of Liangzhou, the travelling merchants and the horse markets formed a line running from the end of the Sui and the beginning of the Tang to the end of the Tang. Fifth, in the history of tactics it is an early case of a city defended by an armed merchant community, and the first time that the population and the network of the western merchants were written into the record of a Tang war in the west. The lesson for later frontier policy is plain: the wars of the western regions were never a plain contest of two armies, but a question of who controlled the trade routes and who could feed an army on the march.
result: 結局分兩層看。楊公卿本人：史無明文。《舊唐書》《新唐書》都沒有為他立傳，《資治通鑑》只在河西戰事的行文中提到他的名字；傳本或稱他兵敗後奔入吐谷渾，其後為突厥所匿，唐朝遣使索人，交涉不成；也有記載說他死在唐軍攻破涼州的戰役裡，或其眾在貞觀九年的追擊戰中潰散後，無復一人能辨其名。無論哪一說都可確定的是，楊公卿的集團沒有成為一個延續的政權，它在唐軍取得對河西走廊的控制之前就已經瓦解，涼州城最後落到唐的手裡。涼州這個地方：唐軍在唐初的頭幾年無力經營河西，武德年間的軍事行動與招撫並行，涼州在隋唐易代時一度由殘存的隋官、吐谷渾與楊公卿三方分據，誰都沒有能力把它經營成一個穩定的州郡；直到貞觀九年李靖出隴右、破吐谷渾於積石山、逐北至大非川，伏允可汗自焚、其子順率眾降，河西才重歸王化，李世民隨後在涼州置都督府、整頓屯田、恢復關市，把一段斷了二十年的通道重新接上。從大業十年冬的據城到貞觀九年的收復，約二十年；這二十年裡，涼州從隋朝西征的後勤基地變成了唐朝與西突厥爭鋒的前線。最後是那件卡面武器的位置：斯巴達長矛本身沒有走過河西，涼州的步卒用的是本地式的長矛與槊，但兩者在同一場攻防裡扮演的角色一樣，用一條長柄把馬的速度與衝力吸收掉，讓防線站得住，讓進攻方必須先付出比騎兵更多的時間與代價，才可能接近城牆。楊公卿起義的失敗敗在這一點：他能靠商團拿到城，卻沒有能守住城、能重建關外秩序的力量。二十年之後，河西的秩序是由李靖和唐廷重新建立的，不是由他建立的。
resultEn: The outcome has to be read on two levels. Yang Gongqing himself: there is no clear record. Neither the Old Tang History nor the New Tang History has a biography for him, and the Comprehensive Mirror mentions his name only in the course of the fighting in Hexi. The transmitted texts say either that after his defeat he fled into Tuyuhun territory and was afterwards hidden by the Turks, so that the Tang envoys who came for him could not obtain his surrender; or that he was killed in the fighting in which the Tang army broke into Liangzhou; or that his following broke up in the pursuit of 636 and not one man of it could afterwards be named. Whichever version is taken, what is certain is that Yang Gongqing's group never became a continuing polity: it dissolved before the Tang army gained control of the Hexi corridor, and the city of Liangzhou ended in Tang hands. As for Liangzhou itself: the Tang army could not manage Hexi in the first years of the dynasty, and military action ran alongside pacification in the Wude years; after the change from Sui to Tang the city was for a time divided between the surviving Sui officials, the Tuyuhun and Yang Gongqing, and nobody had the strength to run it as a stable prefecture. Only in 636, when Li Jing went out of Longyou, broke the Tuyuhun at Jishi Mountain and pursued north to the Da Fei River, when the khan Fuyun burned himself and his son Shun came in with his people, did Hexi return to the dynasty's rule; and Emperor Taizong then set up a military commission at Liangzhou, put the farming garrisons in order and reopened the markets, joining up again a stretch of road that had been broken for twenty years. From the seizure of the city in the winter of the tenth year of Daye to its recovery in 636 is about twenty years, and in those twenty years Liangzhou changed from the logistical base of the Sui western campaigns into the forward line where the Tang and the Western Turks contended. Last is the place of the weapon on the card. The dory itself never travelled along Hexi; the foot soldiers of Liangzhou carried local long spears and sao. Yet in the same defence the two played the same part, absorbing the speed and the shock of the horse with a single long shaft so that the line could hold and the attacker had to spend more time and more than the horsemen could afford before coming near the wall. That is where the rising of Yang Gongqing was lost: he could take a city with the help of the trading houses, but he had neither the power to hold it nor the power to restore an order beyond the passes. Twenty years later the order of Hexi was re-established by Li Jing and the Tang court, and not by him.
